sections.overview: This North American hawk moth belongs to the family Sphingidae.
sections.identification: Its grey-brown wings span about 7–8.5 cm.
sections.habitat: It ranges across Canada and the northeastern United States.
sections.diet: Larvae feed on woody plants; black ash is a reported host.
sections.behavior: Adults fly from May to September; southern populations may have two broods.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillar is a hornworm and pupates after larval growth.
sections.ecology: The French common name is sphinx du Canada. It ranges from Canada south to Arkansas. Its congener Sphinx chisoya extends from south Texas into Mexico.
